  • 呈現 Hasan、Asmongold 等知名主播的提名風波，以及觀眾對評選公平性的質疑。
  • 深入說明 Peanut 再度入圍最佳 VTuber後，如何引發 VTuber 社群對身分認同與獎項代表性的論戰。

摘要

頒獎典禮前的風波與制度調整

作者介紹由知名實況主 QTCinderella 創辦的 Streamer Awards。這場頒獎典禮被部分人視為直播界的奧斯卡，也有人批評它像是主播彼此捧場的圈內活動。2025 年典禮曾因台上玩笑、得獎者發言，以及音效、鏡頭等製作問題受到批評；QTCinderella 因此表示，團隊已從經驗中學習，2026 年將進行改進。

今年最明顯的改變之一，是開放創作者自行提名：實況主可登入帳號、選擇獎項類別、上傳直播片段，並向評審說明自己適合入圍的理由。新制度公布後，Hasan 在直播中自薦年度實況主、最佳閒聊實況主及「獨特」獎，也呼籲粉絲前往官方網站投票。作者另提到，今年的獎盃遭竊，但提供的內容尚未進一步說明事件經過。

Hasan 入圍引發公平性疑問

10 月 16 日公布候選名單後，Hasan 發現自己入圍「獨特」獎，反應格外興奮。該獎項表揚內容風格、表演方式或創意方向特別的創作者；Hasan 直播時對著愛犬 Fish 急速發表長篇評論，也成了網友調侃的焦點。部分觀眾認為，他和曾遭虐待動物指控的創作者同列候選，格外諷刺；另一些人則不滿 Asmongold 連續兩年未獲提名，進而質疑名單安排，甚至猜測得獎者是否早已內定，尤其 Hasan 與 QTCinderella 私交甚篤。

Hasan 也談到自己與 Ludwig 的關係。兩人過去曾因 Hasan 對 Kaya 的言論而起爭執，但 Hasan 表示仍期待在典禮上見到 Ludwig，並稱欣賞他的內容。這番話引來觀眾揶揄。另有觀眾要求 Hasan 談政治，他則抱怨社群逐漸難以親近，並指出 Asmongold 能吸引較多一般觀眾，是因為他也談遊戲、流行文化等娛樂內容；Hasan 還提到，美國期中選舉後可能暫時減少政治相關內容。

Peanut 再度入圍最佳 VTuber

最佳 VTuber 候選名單則因 Peanut 再度入圍而掀起另一場論戰。Peanut 以花生造型的虛擬角色直播，曾在去年贏得該獎；但他多次表示自己不認為是 VTuber，還曾以「Peautuber」形容自己的風格，並批評 VTuber 文化只是「賣性感」，因此令不少 VTuber 粉絲不滿。支持者則認為，只要使用虛擬形象直播，就符合 VTuber 的定義；IronMouse 當時也曾表示，針對 Peanut 的批評讓她感到不舒服。

Peanut 今年再次入圍後，創作者 Camila 發文指出，Peanut 雖然很有影響力，卻不認同 VTuber 身分，也曾負面評論相關社群，因此希望他考慮退選，把機會留給真正認同 VTuber 身分的創作者。這番呼籲反而招來批評，甚至有網友表示原本沒有打算投給 Peanut，如今決定支持他。Peanut 則以嘲諷方式回應，開玩笑說要替角色做隆乳與臀部整形手術，暗示自己會迎合大眾對 VTuber 形象的想像。

英文 VTuber Silvervale 預測 Peanut 很可能再次得獎，屆時爭議恐怕會持續延燒；但她也認為，VTuber 社群不斷為一個不重視該社群的頒獎典禮爭論，並無助益，只會讓整個圈子顯得更加難堪。影片在此處轉向另一個受到關注的話題，但提供的字幕未包含後續內容。

for charity. Are you? Why wouldn't you? He appealed to Los Angeles residents, asking anyone who sees the trophies at pawn shops or second-hand stores to let him know. This bizarre situation had many fans. joking that the thieves would be incredibly disappointed when they realized what they had snatched— expecting an iPad, only to find twelve golden Pepe frogs inside. 橫空出世的恐怖傳奇：《P.T.》的震撼登場

dim corridors and even encounter a giant baby that gave many players nightmares. other fan-made remakes, this one uses reverse engineering to rebuild the game's engine and rendering system, restoring the original scenes, sound effects, and puzzle flow as accurately as possible. Regarding the stir that reverse engineering has caused in the gaming world, the creator "Jimi" has made a video about it in the past; interested players can go check it out. However , as the project received more attention , LavenZavier also began to face attacks from some players, with some even accusing him of faking it and sending him terrifying threats. " I want it. >> Just as players were eagerly awaiting the official release of Silent Hills, events took a turn that nobody wanted. Less than a year after P.T. launched, the relationship between Hideo Kojima and Konami had completely deteriorated. In truth, tensions had been building since the development of Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain. As internal restructuring began, Kojima Productions. faced various restrictions; staff were even cut off from company internet, email, and phone access. Hideo Kojima’s own status within the company shifted from a permanent employee to something akin to a contractor. Meanwhile, Kojima’s name gradually vanished from promotional materials, and even the studio’s logo was removed. However, some players still refused to believe it, until April 2015 when Guillermo del Toro confirmed at an event that the collaboration on Silent Hills would not be moving forward, leaving him... ...and Norman Reedus expressed their own regrets on Twitter. As the news spread, it was officially confirmed that Silent Hills would no longer be in development . But it wasn't just the cancellation; Konami actually pulled P.T. from the PlayStation Store. Even worse, players who had already added it to their libraries couldn't redownload it; once you deleted it or switched consoles, it was gone forever. Consequently, people began auctioning off PS4 consoles with P.T. installed on the secondhand market , with prices skyrocketing to thousands of dollars—a reminder that while the.

game was free when it was playable, it cost a fortune when it wasn't. As for why Konami pulled P.T., officials only stated that the game’s licensing period on the PlayStation Store was ending. However, players pointed to a line of dialogue after beating P.T. that sounded as if Hideo Kojima was secretly... Ko-. -nami. Thus, some players speculated that this line, mirroring reality, infuriated Konami, leading them to decide to take P.T. down. The disappearance of P.T. also led many developers to attempt to create works with similar styles, hoping. to recreate that suffocating horror experience. Titles like Allison Road and The Peterson Case drew attention for their resemblance to P.T., yet none of them were ever officially released. During this time, a 17-year-old fan personally created a remake called P.T. for PC, but the project was ultimately shut down by Konami due to legal issues , forcing him to stop development and take it offline. However, this fan also mentioned that a Konami representative told him that many people within the company actually liked his work. In addition to sending him some game merchandise, they even offered him an internship at Konami, which was a very. special experience for him while he was still in high school. As for other players, upon learning their anticipated game was canceled, they vented their anger directly at Konami. The iconic slogan of that time could be seen everywhere on Twitter, forums, and video titles. Even Guillermo del Toro later replied "F***Konami" when Hideo Kojima commemorated the eighth anniversary of P.T., showing their dissatisfaction was no less than the players '. But no matter how much the players protested, there was no turning back; Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain ultimately became Hideo Kojima's final work at Konami. Ironically, not only did this.

game receive acclaim from many players, but it also won the Best Action/ Adventure game award at TGA 2015. However, it wasn't Kojima himself who went on stage to accept the award, but the voice actor for Venom Snake. At the time, TGA host Geoff Keighley explained directly to the audience that Hideo Kojima had received a notice from Konami's lawyers before the ceremony, stating that he was not allowed to attend that night. award >> After leaving, Kojima did not stop there . Just as the lines in P.T. suggested, he formed Kojima Productions with his core team and returned to players with brand-new works. Meanwhile, Konami continued to focus on other business ventures, leaving the Silent Hill series dormant for a long time until recent years, when they finally announced remakes and new projects to bring it back into the public eye. Although it was tragically pulled from stores, the. impact it had on the entire gaming industry was significant. It forced many developers to rethink the storytelling methods and immersion of first-person psychological horror games, using cramped spaces and subtle, unsettling environmental changes to build psychological terror that doesn't just rely on jumpscares. Therefore, apart from fan-made remakes, there are actually many horror games on the market inspired by P.T. For example, the developers of Layers of Fear explicitly stated that P.T. showed them the market demand for psychological horror; instead of just having monsters chase players, they preferred to create fear through. the environment, atmosphere, and constantly shifting scenes. The once-viral "Exit 8" is a horror game that traps players in a constantly looping underground passage, forcing them to carefully observe their surroundings and turn back the moment they spot anything unusual. Although its gameplay isn't exactly the same as P.T. , the developer mentioned that P.T. was indeed one of the inspirations for the game. In addition, the development team behind Resident Evil Village didn't explicitly state that P.T. was an inspiration, but in the Beneviento House level, players are not only stripped of their weapons but also forced to explore.

dim corridors and even encounter a giant baby that gave many players nightmares. This design, which deliberately deprives players of security and uses the environment and psychological pressure to create fear, reminded many players and industry insiders of P.T. What the freak? P.T. >> Hideo Kojima surely never imagined that the name of a game he helped develop would become an adjective; another adjective I know is "Discord." Interestingly, the influence of this work even extended to the world of adult. games. For example, an adult game called "Chain Wolf" tasks players with avoiding a massive monster in a looping space, where being caught leads to big trouble . Plus, just looking at the opening scene of the game, players know exactly which game it was inspired by without needing to be told. Even though I'm trembling, as a gentleman, I'm still a bit excited. Is this what they call "if you're brave enough, even a ghost can ..."? Comeback. Before we knew it, it's already 2026, and what neither the gaming community nor Hideo Kojima expected was that he would face a situation similar to the one he had back at Konami. This time,. Sony announced its withdrawal from developing the action-espionage game " Physint" with Kojima Productions, once leaving the project on the verge of being canceled. Regarding this incident , I have already made a video sharing it , so interested players can go check it out. Fortunately, this project was luckier. After Sony pulled out, Kojima Productions actively sought new partners , and ultimately, Xbox took over publishing, allowing "Physint" to continue development. Long before that, Hideo Kojima had actually been working with Xbox to develop another horror game , also consisting of two letters: "OD." Seeing Hideo Kojima return to the horror. genre, many fans are naturally excited and expectant, hoping to see a P.T.- level horror experience in this game. However, with the precedent from back then, many players are starting to get PTSD, worrying that Xbox might pull something similar in the future, with many joking that "OD" actually stands for "Only Demo"— "Remember to download the demo, and whatever you do, don't delete it.""I guess we can only blame Hideo Kojima for being bad at naming horror games; he should have called it FR, then players would believe the game could FRelease." To the surprise of many , a developer named LavenZavier recently succeeded in porting the long-discontinued P.T. to PC. Unlike.

other fan-made remakes, this one uses reverse engineering to rebuild the game's engine and rendering system, restoring the original scenes, sound effects, and puzzle flow as accurately as possible. Regarding the stir that reverse engineering has caused in the gaming world, the creator "Jimi" has made a video about it in the past; interested players can go check it out. The news quickly gained support from many players, and even renowned game data miner Lance McDonald gave high praise to the fidelity of this port. What was even more unexpected for LavenZavier was that Kojima himself noticed the project and retweeted a. report introducing this port, leaving LavenZavier incredibly thrilled. However , as the project received more attention , LavenZavier also began to face attacks from some players, with some even accusing him of faking it and sending him terrifying threats. Facing this malicious feedback, he stated that he would significantly reduce the time spent on the project; while he might release fixes and updates in the future , he no longer promises continuous active development. This led some players to speculate that LavenZavier's porting project might have impacted the collector's value of PS4 consoles that still have P.T. installed, which is why some people attacked him. Although many. players are unhappy with those attacking the developer, others believe that the fact LavenZavier enabled more players to experience P.T. on PC is already very meaningful. P.T. was originally just a free demo intended to tease Silent Hills , but unexpectedly, with its unique horror experience, it not only became a classic in horror game history but also influenced the design of many later games. Even though Hideo Kojima and Konami have parted ways, players still haven't forgotten this work, and developers are even striving to let more people experience the original P.T. on PC. One can only hope the upcoming OD makes it to an official release and. isn't just a "lyDemo." I wonder what you , the players, think about the story behind P.T.? 值得閱讀的理由

  • 深入了解知名虛擬實境平台 VRChat 在生成式 AI 浪潮下所面臨的原創生態衝擊與治理挑戰。
  • 剖析高達 95% 玩家要求標註 AI 內容，官方卻以「缺乏共識」為由全盤否決的荒謬決策與公關危機。
  • 探討數位創作平台上「內容透明度」、「創作者權益」與「消費者知情選擇權」之間的激烈交鋒。

摘要

生成式 AI 浪潮衝擊 VRChat 創作生態

作者指出，作為一個高度依賴玩家自製內容（UGC）的知名 VR 社交平台，VRChat 原本由社群心血建構的虛擬生態正遭受生成式 AI 的巨大衝擊。隨著 AI 門檻降低，平台上充斥著大量低成本且低品質的生成內容，甚至有創作者利用華麗的 AI 宣傳圖欺騙玩家點擊，嚴重擠壓了耗費數月心血的手工創作者之曝光空間。相較於 Pixiv 與 Steam 等平台早已推出 AI 標籤或強制揭露機制，VRChat 官方遲遲未有作為，引發海外社群強烈不滿，創作者與志工甚至發起抵制並在作品加上粉紅色的 NoAI 標籤進行抗議。

社群施壓促成官方調查，民調高達九成五支持標籤

面對社群日益擴大的反彈聲浪，VRChat 官方隨後公開回應，承認 AI 帶來粗製濫造內容的隱憂，但也認為 AI 在代碼輔助與多語言翻譯上具有正面效益。為了制定合適政策，官方發起了一份為期七天的問卷調查，迅速收集到超過兩萬份回饋與深度訪談。調查中最引人注目的結果顯示，有高達 95% 的玩家明確支持平台應為 AI 生成內容增設標籤與分類過濾功能，讓社群原以為這項訴求已成定局。

官方以缺乏共識為由拒推標籤，引發社群一片譁然

出乎所有人意料的是，官方最終做出了斷然拒絕的決策。官方搬出數據辯解，稱玩家在面對多種 AI 使用情境時提出了超過三千種標籤組合，彼此間毫無共識，且僅有約三分之一的玩家表示會刻意避開 AI 內容；此外，官方還擔心標籤制度會引發社群「獵巫」式的騷擾行為。作者與廣大玩家對這種推託說詞感到無比震驚，社群紛紛以「沙漠中 95% 的人渴望喝水，卻因要用杯子或瓶子裝沒有共識，官方決定讓所有人渴死」等尖銳寓言，強烈諷刺官方為了迎合投資者而忽視廣大民意。

核心爭議在於「知情權」與「自由選擇權」

作者總結指出，玩家社群自始至終並非要求全面封殺 AI 技術，而是要求最基本的透明度與消費者的知情選擇權。許多創作者強調，官方大可先推出初步的標籤版本並逐步調整，而非以追求完美方案或防範獵巫為藉口直接擺爛。每位使用者都有權根據自身的價值觀決定是否支持包含 AI 的作品，而 VRChat 官方完全扼殺選擇權的消極做法，最終只換來了社群的大量負評與信任危機。

================================================

As everyone knows, surveys allow players to provide feedback, which developers then collect and analyze to improve the gaming experience and adjust operational strategies. Simply put, it’s a crucial way to extend a game's lifespan and retain players. Now, suppose you were a social platform developer. If you learned that 95%of your players wanted the platform to label AI-generated content, would you meet their demands? Hello, everyone, and welcome to Player Files. As a free massive multiplayer online VR. social platform, VRChat realized the metaverse Mark Zuckerberg dreamed of long before Meta spent tens of billions of dollars only to crash and burn. While it's a social game on the surface , it's actually an emotional lubricant. Mommy's little boy. I love you. Love you too. >> Are you ready to take it to the next level? >> However, four years ago, the developers stirred up massive player resentment and review-bombed Steam when they implemented the EAC anti-cheat tool to block malicious mods without prior communication, effectively banning all mods in the process. Unexpectedly, four years later, the developers did communicate, and they knew exactly what the players wanted. After reflecting in silence for a few weeks, they made a bold decision to reject the players 'request—as swiftly and painlessly as being rejected by my VR crush. Such a bold move, unsurprisingly, left players feeling " impressed," and then they left negative. reviews. So, what exactly happened? Next , Player Files will share the recent controversy with you all. If there’s anything we missed or anything you'd like to add, feel free to leave a comment below. Before we start the video, don't forget to like and subscribe to our channel, and make sure to ring the bell so you don't miss our updates. Besides socializing, one of VRChat’s biggest features is that a massive amount of content is handmade by players . Many creators build their own virtual worlds or avatars for players worldwide to visit and interact in. However, with.

the rise of AI technology, this virtual ecosystem originally built by players is facing new challenges. By just inputting a few lines of text, you can use AI to generate images, concept art, and scene assets, or even assist in making 3D models and writing code. This has led some players to worry that the platform will be flooded with low-cost, low-quality AI content. Some people even use AI to create flashy promotional images, only for players to enter the world and find that the actual content falls short of the screenshots. More importantly, when huge amounts of content can be generated rapidly, creators who spend months building. high-quality worlds may find it even harder to get discovered. Of course, this isn't a problem unique to VR. Other platforms faced similar controversies long ago and have since rolled out their own solutions. For example, the famous Japanese illustration platform pixiv added tags for AI-generated works, allowing users to choose whether to show or hide them during searches. But for an eager learner like me, whether it’s hand-drawn or AI-generated, I still have to take a good, close look at them. As for Steam, which gamers love so much, although they don't offer a feature to filter out AI games, they began requiring developers in 2024 to disclose. their use of generative AI in games, letting players know what they are getting into before buying so they can decide whether to support them. In contrast, VRChat has been slow to introduce features for users to identify or filter out the growing amount of AI content on the platform. As a result, overseas players and creators have started to speak up, hoping the official team will take this issue seriously. One VRChat community volunteer, Pat, even publicly announced they would pause their involvement in VRChat translation , Wiki maintenance, and community testing, and started a group to call on others to join the boycott. Not only. that, they encouraged everyone to add " NoAI" to their works, hoping to put pressure on the official team in this way. Soon, other creators responded, and pink "NoAI" tags started appearing on various world thumbnails in VRChat. Facing increasing community pressure, VRChat......quickly responded publicly to the matter. The officials acknowledged that AI is a current issue for the platform and understand that generative AI could bring a flood of low-quality, low-effort works, further affecting the platform's creative ecosystem. However, they also believe AI.

is not without its benefits; after all, some creators use AI to assist with coding and translating different languages, allowing their work to be better and reach players in more regions . So, it mainly comes down to how those people use AI. Therefore, VRChat does not want to dismiss all creators who use AI just because some AI-generated content is of poor quality. To address this, they proposed several directions, including updating creator guidelines to prohibit the use of world thumbnails that mislead players. In other words, regardless of whether an image is AI-generated, if a player enters a world and finds the content doesn't match the promotional image, it may violate. platform guidelines. Actually, you don't even need to go in to find the difference; the various AI-generated food images and posters in real life are already enough for a nerd like me to tell whether something is an AI image. >> My AI radar is very sharp. The official team also plans to improve the discovery and recommendation systems for worlds and avatars, giving well-crafted works more exposure while allowing players to provide feedback directly in-game, so creators know how their work is being received. As for the most discussed topic—AI and AI content filtering—the officials couldn't make a decision. They feel it's not impossible, but they don't. know how to distinguish between different levels of AI usage or under what circumstances creators should be required to disclose their use of AI. So , they decided to continue communicating with the community and created a survey , giving players seven days to provide their suggestions. In just seven short days, this survey received over 20,000 responses. To better understand how different players view AI, the officials also conducted one-on-one interviews with some creators. The most striking figure from the entire survey was that a staggering 95%of players want the platform to add AI tags. Just when the player community thought this was a sure. win, the officials had more to say. Although a huge number of players want AI tags, the officials believe other survey results show this doesn't represent......that players completely reject AI. They then started pulling out a mountain of data to prove that players are actually still accepting of AI-assisted creation. For instance, when asked how to label works for eight different AI usage scenarios, players proposed over 3,000 different tag combinations, with none receiving more than 10%support. Therefore, the officials argue that while most players want more.

transparency regarding AI use, there is no consensus on when to tag or how to categorize them. Wait, how did the player community become the ones responsible for solving this problem? Furthermore, they pointed out that only 33%of players said they would deliberately avoid AI-assisted content, and among those who left written feedback, only 37%expressed similar views. Regardless of all that, it doesn't change the fact that 95%of players want AI tags, so many players expected the. officials to meet the majority's needs. To everyone's surprise, VRChat ultimately decided not to launch AI tags or provide AI content filtering. Wish I could, but I can't. Well, I could , but I won't, maybe, but in short—no. >> This decision left many players feeling completely stunned. Having put effort into filling out the survey, it backfired, only making the officials more confused about why tags are even needed. Content creators have pointed out that players have clearly expressed their desire for the platform to add AI labels. As for how these labels should be designed, they could easily release. an initial version and adjust it based on player feedback, rather than doing nothing at all just because they can't find a solution that satisfies everyone . Many players have sarcastically quipped, "95%of survey respondents want AI usage to be labeled in some way, but that’s not what our investors want to see, so you’ll just have to keep consuming this junk content—and you’ll like it, too. What a shame.""95%of people in the desert want water, but some want it in a cup, some want it bottled, some want a tap, and others want it in a kettle. Ultimately, we conclude that the desert residents want to die of thirst, because they couldn't. reach a consensus on how to get water, so we won't give it to them." However, there are other reasons why officials are refusing to introduce AI labels. Since labels rely on creator self-reporting, they worry that some might be dishonest, and they also fear that AI labels could trigger new forms of community harassment, with some players acting like detectives to hunt down works suspected of using AI and harassing the creators. Why does this sound so familiar? The person who said this seems to have been mocked by quite a few players. Nevertheless, many players believe these reasons are simply not enough to serve as an excuse for.

refusing to increase transparency. After all, what players have been asking for from the start isn't a ban on AI works on the platform, but for the platform to provide them with a choice. Content creators have pointed out that consumers need to know if a product uses AI so that everyone can make choices based on their own values; in this regard, Steam is still far ahead. Some don't mind AI, while others don't want to engage with AI-generated content ; that is a consumer's freedom. Therefore, he believes that using potential harassment as an excuse to deny a consumer-friendly transparency feature is just an attempt to shirk responsibility. He even criticized this behavior not as cowardice, but as a deliberate attempt to use any excuse possible to avoid doing the right thing. >> As for the AI content filtering feature , officials argue that once players set up filter criteria, they might miss out. on that content forever. This explanation was similarly blasted by players, who stated that they are setting the filters precisely because they don't want to see that content. Although the officials refused to implement an AI tag, they lean toward using a "Human-Made" label, allowing creators who don't use AI to identify their work as human-made. At the same time, to better understand the boundaries of AI labeling, they are conducting a single-question survey, asking players to help them answer it. Wait, didn't you just say that you refused to launch an AI tag because you were worried creators would hide their AI usage? Following that logic, if I use. AI to create, can't I also just mark my own work as human-made? Consequently, this method, which also appears to have loopholes, naturally makes many players feel that it cannot effectively solve the problem of information transparency . Because they didn't listen to the 95% of players, and even their provided explanation failed to convince the community, VRChat quickly drew heavy criticism. Players felt the officials didn't respect their opinions at all, and the selective ignoring of the statistics they provided left players questioning the point of asking for community input in the first place. Some sarcastically mocked VRChat for protecting low-quality AI-generated.

content, even quipping, "I didn't know TamSwiny was on your board of directors . We wanted you to fill out the survey, not answer it like this." Furthermore, to express their dissatisfaction, some players even unsubscribed from VRChat Plus and called on others to vote with their wallets. On the day the officials announced the survey results and their final decision , those 95%of players quickly went to Steam to leave negative reviews. Currently, the positive rating in the English-speaking region has already fallen to 30%. Even the Halloween event. VRChat originally planned to host was affected, with two DJs publicly announcing their withdrawal from the event due to dissatisfaction with the official decision. Interestingly, since the officials refused to use an AI tag, the players decided to do it themselves . Because Steam's community tagging system isn't just for game developers— as long as players have a qualified, unrestricted account, they can add tags to games themselves. Steam then sorts them by tag weight, and only the top 20 tags are displayed on the store page, so dissatisfied players started mass-tagging it as AI. As a result, on. November 1st, an "Artificial Intelligence" tag actually appeared on VRChat's Steam store page for a time, and Steam won without doing anything because they had long provided a feature for players to tag games themselves. However, the tag only lasted for about a day before disappearing, and the reason remains unclear. Although VRChat's refusal to add AI tags might be due to concerns about predatory behavior, it’s quite abstract to ignore a survey where 95%of users want the feature. One can only hope the game finds a solution that satisfies player needs without compromising the experience. What are your thoughts on the recent controversies surrounding VRChat?
